item.title: Negative Space, Positive Reception: Other Things Uttered by Hayes Prize Recipient Tommy Kha
item.description: Thoughtful conversation unfolded throughout the Addison Gallery of American Art (Addison) last Thursday evening as the space hosted a book release party celebrating “Other Things Uttered,” the catalog accompanying artist-in-residence Tommy Kha’s first solo museum exhibition. The reception marked both the long-awaited arrival of the publication and an unofficial, bittersweet closing to an exhibition that has shaped artistic and academic conversations on campus over the past year. item.title: The Identity Show: How Experiences Shape Us
item.description: The Identity Show had its third and final run on Monday, January 19 in the Pan Athletic Center. The show was a culmination of individually written pieces surrounding unique aspects of the performers’ identities, originally debuted in the Fall Term. Performers workshopped to bring the show to Andover, channeling years of lived experiences into an emotional display of human stories. item.title: Daisy Lopez Vargas ’26’s CaMD Scholar Presentation Unpacks Lived History of U.S.-Mexico Migration
item.description: Daisy Lopez Vargas ’26 delivered her Community and Multicultural Development (CAMD) presentation, titled “Do I Run? Swim? Climb?,” on Martin Luther King Jr. (MLK) Day. Through firsthand interviews and historical documentation, Lopez’s presentation explored the stories of migrants and their experiences crossing the border between Mexico and the U.S. For her project, Lopez focused on documenting migrants living in Los Angeles, California, where she grew up. item.description: Dr. Kiran Bhardwaj is an Instructor and Chair of the Philosophy and Religious Studies Department as well as a House Counselor in Double Brick House. item.title: James Wilkerson Speaks on Male Mental Health
item.description: James Wilkerson, Associate Dean of Students at Indiana University Southeast, delivered the talk “When We Cry: Navigating Male Mental Health” to Juniors, Upper, and Seniors for this Winter Term’s EBI meeting. Wilkerson explored masculinity norms, the impacts of societal expectations, and the importance of emotional well-being. item.title: Students Comment on Annual Mid-Year Reflection
item.description: Midway through Winter Term each year, Andover students complete a written reflection titled “A Letter to the Adults in my Life,” where they reflect on their past year’s experience. Following the reflection, students meet with their point person to discuss the reflection, which is eventually shared with parents and made available to campus adults. item.title: Tessa Hulls Presents Pulitzer-Winning Graphic Memoir “Feeding Ghosts”
item.description: Tessa Hulls, Pulitzer Prize-winning author of “Feeding Ghosts: A Graphic Memoir,” held a writers’ workshop and lecture last Friday in Kemper as part of Mixed Heritage Awareness Week (MHAW). Hulls spoke on her struggles with her mixed identity, gender roles in American society, and how she uses graphic novels to express her emotions and life story. Drawing inspiration from her own family history, Hulls explored how she expresses her identity as an individual of both Chinese and American heritage

item.title: Chasing Dreams: José Hernández Reflects on Perseverance During MLK Day ASM
item.description: José Hernández, an engineer and former NASA astronaut, took the stage of Cochran Chapel during All-School Meeting (ASM) honoring Martin Luther King Jr. (MLK) Day. In his talk, Hernández detailed his life story and career path, urging students to view their dreams not as distant ideals but as goals achievable through effort and self-discipline. item.title: Thirty-Sixth Head of School Day Announced Ahead of Forecasted Snowstorm
item.description: Head of School Raynard Kington announced on Friday evening in Paresky Commons that the Thirty-Sixth Head of School Day (HOSD) will take place on Monday, January 26. The announcement was followed later that night by a campus-wide email from Susan Esty, Dean of Students and Residential Life, confirming that all classes, athletics, and interscholastic practices will be cancelled on Monday.
